the_correction.why_that_was_not_a_rate: four instances, three of them hand-picked from repositories whose languages and idioms I had just studied. A 75% on N=4 has a confidence interval from roughly 30% to 95%.
the_correction.this_round: a miner that builds instances automatically from upstream fix commits, proves two controls on each, deduplicates by patch, and runs the engine over the corpus
the_correction.the_direction: down, substantially. That is the honest direction.

the_miner.note_on_FIX_CONTROL_NOT_GREEN: the largest single rejection class. These are commits whose own suite does not go green in this environment -- missing optional deps, platform-specific tests, or a fix that depends on a library version not installed. They are rejected, never counted.

the_evaluation.note: both solves came from one crystallised skill learned on the first jinja bug. Without a warm skill store the engine would have solved one.

three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.detail: `_raw()` was called with a spec that already began with `repos/`, and the function prefixed it again to `repos/repos/...`. GitHub returned 404, the exception handler returned None, and the commit was rejected as PARENT_UNRECOVERABLE.
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.impact: every changed file inside a large module was silently unrecoverable. click's core.py is 149 KB and produced no body from the contents API, so this path was common, not rare.
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.class: an error whose rejection reason is wrong -- the exact failure mode this project legislates against
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.fix: normalise the path once, and fall through to the git blobs API for large files

three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.detail: urllib had no token and failed on some responses; `gh` carries ambient credentials
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.impact: a transport failure was indistinguishable from a missing file
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.fix: fall back to `gh api` before concluding a file cannot be read

three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.bug: dedupe keyed on the wrong field
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.detail: the first dedupe keyed on (repo, revert_control, first src file), which merged two DIFFERENT jinja bugs because both produced `53 passed 1 failed`; a later key included the sha, which merged nothing at all
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.impact: the denominator swung between 8 and 14 for the same data
three_bugs_i_found_in_my_own_harness_thi.fix: fingerprint the recovered parent patch text. Two commits that revert to identical source are one bug; two fixes to the same file are not.

the_positive_control.why_it_is_essential: with the engine at 22% one cannot tell whether the corpus is outside its reach or the rig is broken. The positive control proves the rig works and the misses are the engine's expressible-set limit.
the_positive_control.status_before_this_round: known solved in the previous round; re-verified this round

click_8c73ff13.experiment: applied the four edits of the true upstream fix one at a time and re-ran the oracle
click_8c73ff13.the_remaining_five_failures: need a rewritten f-string plus a new isinstance branch, a list comprehension over envvars, a join with per-item quoting, and a changed assignment
click_8c73ff13.conclusion: this fix REQUIRES statement insertion. The engine's mutator replaces spans in place. No combination of in-place replacements reaches it, because the function must gain statements it does not have.

why_the_misses_fail__measured_not_assume.the_general_limit: the engine expresses repairs as a replacement of one AST span. Every miss in this corpus needs either (a) more than one span, or (b) statements the source does not contain. That is a hypothesis-space limit, not an effort limit -- the same finding ARC produced, in a different domain.

the_law_answer__repriced.the_question: what is most important and most valuable in this project, and how valuable is it
the_law_answer__repriced.what_changed: the SWE repair engine was ranked second on a 75% figure. At 22% on a control-verified corpus it is still the most valuable ENGINE, but its value is now correctly stated: it solves single-span bugs on foreign code reliably and multi-statement refactors not at all.
the_law_answer__repriced.rank_1: 780 action-intent laws with falsification conditions -- unchanged, still the most valuable artefact
the_law_answer__repriced.rank_2: the SWE repair engine -- 22.2% on 9 unique control-verified upstream bugs, 100% on single-span bugs, 0% on multi-statement refactors, 0 model calls, $0
the_law_answer__repriced.rank_5: the self-falsification records -- including this one

what_is_still_NOT_real: no SWE-bench Verified score. Nine unique bugs across three small Python libraries is a real rate on real code and a small sample from a narrow repository population.

the 22.2% is not comparable to any published SWE-bench number: different repositories, different oracle construction, different bug distribution, and a corpus that excludes every bug the engine cannot express the fix for only because the suite happened not to be green in this environment.
the_next_frontier__now_measured: statement insertion. The engine needs a mechanism that can author new statements (an isinstance branch, a comprehension, a join) rather than replace an existing span. That is a concrete, testable target: on this corpus it is worth 5 of the 7 misses, and its success criterion is a green suite, not a benchmark claim.
